examples.explanation: The substitutive name ethaneperoxol is the preferred IUPAC name; ethyl hydroperoxide is the functional-class form shown in the source.
The new SO-thioperoxol suffix replaces the discarded sulfenic acid suffix.
The chalcogen analogue uses the introduced diselenoperoxol suffix rather than the former name.
Imidamide is the functional replacement suffix in the preferred IUPAC name.
Carboximidamide replaces carboxamidine in the preferred IUPAC name.
Methylene is retained and preferred for the -CH2- substituent group.
The double-bonded group uses ylidene; methylidene is the preferred prefix and methylene is the former name.
The single-bonded divalent group uses the diyl ending; ethylene is the older form.
A free-valence double bond is expressed by the ylidene ending.
Silanediyl is the preselected prefix for the single-bonded group; silylene remains a CAS name.
Germylidene is the preselected prefix for the double-bonded group.
Boranediyl is the preselected prefix for the single-bonded group.
Boranylidene is the preselected prefix for the double-bonded group.
Stibanediyl is the preselected prefix; stibinediyl and the CAS name stibylene are not the preferred form.
Stibanylidene is the preselected prefix; stibinylidene and the CAS name stibylene are not the preferred form.
Carbonylbis(azanediyl) is the preferred prefix used in multiplicative nomenclature.

value.scope: suffixes introduced or modified by these recommendations
source_text: Suffixes have always been considered as the most unique elements of the formation of names.
In the past, some suffixes have been discarded and replaced by new ones.
The following suffixes have been introduced or modified in these recommendations.

value.preferred_over: names generated by functional class nomenclature
value.recommendation: use peroxol to provide substitutive names

value.source_text: These suffixes are replaced by the new suffixes; see P-63.4.2.1.

semantic_units.term: diyl and ylidene endings for divalent substituent groups

value.external_usage: CAS still uses ylene for diyl and ylidene bond types, especially methylene for -CH2- and CH2=.
value.former_scope: divalent substituent groups whose free valences do not form a double bond
value.historical_status: discarded in 1993 except for methylene, ethylene, and phenylene
